hook: A 1917 Craftsman bungalow, apparently a Sears "Hollywood", built for a shipwright.

historic_survey.finding: Appears eligible for the California Register under Criterion 1 (events) and Criterion 3 (design and construction)
historic_survey.physical_integrity: Retains location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, feeling and association
historic_survey.note: A one-and-a-half-story bungalow midway up a heavily planted bank, with a broad side-facing gable, a porch the width of the front on paired round columns and sculpted brackets, and a Craftsman oak door. The survey takes it for a Sears and Roebuck mail-order bungalow, Modern Home No. 264p234, "The Hollywood", and calls that a rare thing in San Francisco. The report's narrative dates the house to 1920; its inventory form, its building record and the assessor's roll all give 1917.

historical_record.description: The concrete retaining wall and the stairs up to the house were added.

The Norwegian-born ship builder Ingeborg Jorgenson built the bungalow for a daughter and her husband, the shipwright Fred Siemer of the yard Siemer & Bruer & Co. The house held one of the oldest boat-building families of India Basin, on a lot generous enough to recall the semi-rural conditions that once prevailed at Hunters Point.
